title: Frontend's consignment addresses list shows only the chosen party's name; Design release 1 shows the whole address the trader picked

finding.frontend: Once a party has been chosen, the Consignment addresses page shows the party's name and nothing else. In the captured answered state the five rows read "Astra Rosales", "Tech Imports Ltd", "Origin Farm", "British Livestock Ltd" and "Import Co UK", each beside a "Change" link, with no street, town, postcode or country anywhere on the page. The row value is the record's name alone (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:32-53, which passes `parties[party.id]?.name` as the summary-list value at :49). A trader who has picked the wrong record of two with similar names cannot tell from this page; to check it they have to reopen the picker, because nothing else in the addresses section shows the address again. It reappears only on the check-your-answers page at the end of the journey, which does render every party as a name and a full address.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 prints the selected address in full inside an inset block under each party heading — the name in bold, then every address line, then the postcode and country on the last line, then "Change" (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:59-68). In the captured answered state Place of origin reads Green Valley Farm / Str. Principală nr. 45 / Sat Sânpetru / Comuna Sânpetru / Jud. Brașov / 507190, Romania. The CPH row uses the same inset and prints the number.
finding.difference: Show the selected address, not just the name, in every answered row of the Consignment addresses page: name, then the address lines, then postcode and country. The data is already in reach — the picker's own "View details" expander renders exactly these lines from `detailLines` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:15-22) and the hub already resolves the full party record before rendering (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:55-59). Nothing else has to land first. Note that the frontend's rows are a govuk summary list and Design release 1's are headed sections with an inset; the requirement is that the address is visible, not that the component matches. `controls` is deliberately empty: the difference runs down all six rows of the page, and the only named control on a row, "Change", occurs six times and would be refused a crop anyway.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any address line, town, postcode or country rendered in an answered row of the frontend's Consignment addresses page. The captured DOM of fe-addresses-hub-complete contains none of the address text for any of its six answered rows.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier. Tag-stripped capture/html/frontend/fe-addresses-hub-complete.html and read all six rows: every value cell holds a bare name — Astra Rosales, Tech Imports Ltd, Origin Farm, British Livestock Ltd, Import Co UK, 123456789 — and no street, town, postcode or country appears anywhere in the list. Did the same on capture/html/prototype/dr1-roles-and-addresses-answered.html and got the full inset for every party, ending "507190, Romania" and "Hull, HU9 5PX, United Kingdom". Opened evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-addresses-hub-complete.png and evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-roles-and-addresses.png and read both. Checked the two frontend citations at their lines: parties[party.id]?.name is passed as the row value at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:49 and resolveParties runs before the render at :59, both as claimed. Rubric 2 fired on one clause — see correction. The claim itself stands.
finding.correction: The claim stands; one clause in the frontend slot was overstated and has been fixed. It said the only way to check a chosen address is to reopen the picker. That is true of the addresses section but not of the journey: the tag-stripped capture/html/frontend/fe-check-answers.html renders every party as a name followed by the full address ("Astra Rosales 43 East Hague Extension Bern 30055 Switzerland") under a "Roles and addresses" card, so the address does come back — at the end, after the section is finished, which is exactly where it is no longer useful for catching the mistake. The slot now says that. Two further notes for whoever reads this next. The "wrong Green Valley Farm of two" was an illustration, not an observation — neither fixture holds two records with the same name (the frontend's thirteen are all distinct at src/server/app/services/address-book/stub/index.js:11-24), and a fixture's contents would not be a finding anyway; the point that a name alone does not identify a record is what carries it, so the illustration has been generalised. Second, the unanswered rows differ too, and that is deliberately not part of this finding: Frontend prints "Not added yet" and a link reading "Add", Design release 1 prints no value and a link reading "Add a place of origin". The status word follows from the summary-list component this finding declines to argue about; the link wording does not, and it is raised on its own as addresses--hub-add-links-do-not-name-the-party.
